fields.value: Presented as gentlemanlike and sensible; detailed physical description is not central.
Intelligent, practical, good-humoured, responsible, and quietly generous.
To support his nieces, protect the family during crisis, and act with fairness and discretion.
Mrs Bennet’s brother, a London merchant living in Gracechurch Street; socially and morally more refined than class prejudice predicts.
Not stated; an established married adult.
Practical helper, travelling companion, and corrective to assumptions about trade and gentility.
Husband of Mrs Gardiner; uncle of the Bennet sisters; father of several children.
Helps make the Pemberley encounter possible and takes visible responsibility during Lydia’s crisis while Darcy works privately.
Elizabeth: affectionate uncle and host. Darcy: develops mutual respect. Lydia: helps negotiate the apparent rescue.
Chapter 25 during the Christmas visit to Longbourn.
